name: SQL Server Migration Assessment
description: Captures SQL Server-specific target, compatibility, platform-service, validation, licensing and operating decisions that complement automated discovery.

sections.title: SQL Server Workload & Target
sections.description: Identify database scope, application coupling, service dependencies and the intended target.

questions.text: Which databases are in scope, and must they be migrated as one consistency group?
Are cross-database transactions or three-part object references used by critical applications?
Which SQL Server platform services are business-critical?
Describe maintenance windows, reporting cycles, ETL schedules and month-end constraints.
Which SQL Server migration destination is being evaluated?
options: SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines

sections.title: SQL Server Features & Compatibility
sections.description: Decide how discovered SQL Server capabilities and compatibility constraints will be handled.

questions.text: Which discovered SQL Server features are business-critical, removable or require replacement?
Are linked servers used in synchronous application or reporting flows?
Can SQL Agent jobs, SSIS packages and external scripts be moved to cloud-native orchestration services?
Who owns migration or replacement of SQL Agent, SSIS, SSRS, SSAS and related platform services?
Describe dependencies on instance-level objects such as logins, credentials, proxies, endpoints and server triggers.
Are MSDTC or other distributed transactions required by critical applications?
Have database compatibility level, deprecated features, collation and time-zone dependencies been assessed against the target?

sections.title: Migration & Availability
sections.description: Select the migration workflow and confirm connectivity, continuity and rollback readiness.

questions.text: What migration method is preferred for this SQL Server workload?
Which availability technology is currently part of the recovery design?
Must CDC, replication or downstream transaction-log consumers continue during migration?
Must connection strings remain unchanged after migration?
Has secure connectivity and sustained migration throughput been tested with production-scale data?
Can database and application changes be frozen during final migration and validation?
Describe the rollback method, transaction reconciliation process and rollback decision triggers.

sections.title: Validation & Cutover Readiness
sections.description: Define acceptance evidence, performance thresholds, rehearsals and approvals.

questions.text: Which source-to-target validation checks are required for acceptance?
options: SQL Agent or integration workflow testing

questions.text: Who owns data and transaction reconciliation and can accept documented variances?
Have peak-load baselines and target performance acceptance thresholds been agreed?
options: Baselines captured but thresholds not agreed

questions.text: What is the status of the production-scale migration rehearsal?
Who provides final business, application, database, security and operations sign-off?

sections.title: Security, Licensing & Operations
sections.description: Capture identity, encryption, licensing and post-migration ownership requirements.

questions.text: Which authentication methods must be supported?
Are TDE certificates, column encryption keys or Always Encrypted enclaves in use?
Is an edition or major-version change required, and what licensing constraints apply?
Is Azure Hybrid Benefit or existing SQL Server licensing expected to be used?
Who will own backups, patching, SQL Agent replacement, monitoring and performance tuning after migration?
